1: ---
2: name: rigorous-proof
3: description: Use Yui to make an existing mathematical proof self-contained as structured NL0 with Audit A, then optionally translate it through typed interfaces into Lean with source-faithful Audit B. Supports NL0-only, translation from an accepted NL0, and full workflows. Do not infer proof correctness from schema checks or introduce unproved assumptions to close a goal.
4: ---
5: 
6: # Yui: rigorous proof development
7: 
8: Use the smallest requested track. Preserve the original problem, hypotheses,
9: definitions and proof route. The two stages share one specification and explicit
10: invalidation rules; completing stage one does not require stage two.
11: 
12: The installed skill root is the directory containing this `SKILL.md`. Keep
13: `config.json`, `nl0/`, `nl02lean/` and `toolchain/` beside it; no enclosing
14: `rigorous-proof/` subdirectory or particular checkout name is required.
15: 
16: ## Select a stage
17: 
18: Before dispatch, follow [target selection](nl0/references/target-selection.md).
19: Resolve a clear intended theorem yourself without asking again; ask the user
20: only when the intended target remains ambiguous. Freeze the complete selected
21: statement(s), including standing assumptions, as an explicit job input.
22: 
23: The invoking agent owns request/configuration collection and dispatch. Follow
24: [installed operation](nl0/references/operation.md) to identify explicit proof inputs,
25: ask once for missing active-phase model/reasoning/speed settings and, for a
26: NL0, full or translation request, an explicit per-case worker count N, then call
27: `nl0/scripts/yui.py run` (or prepare/execute). Retain settings already supplied by
28: the user; do not call a separate intent-classification model. Do not silently
29: choose a worker count from defaults or `auto`; obtain a positive integer or
30: the user's explicit confirmation of a proposed number. N bounds local R-node
31: reviews and, in a separate phase, local Lean proofs. NL0/Audit A and
32: Lean preparation/proofs/assembly/Audit B have separate phase profiles. The user
33: does not prepare queues, task packets or controller jobs manually.
34: The invoking owner follows [foreground handoff and monitoring](nl0/references/owner-observation.md):
35: normally dispatch with `--detach`, verify the owned processes, and register one
36: host heartbeat for a bounded check every ten minutes. Record the actual schedule
37: ID, report that mathematical work is still pending, then end the current
38: foreground turn. Never keep the owner active through sleep/poll loops. Each
39: scheduled check ends its turn as well. `DISPATCHED` is not workflow completion.
40: If host scheduling is unavailable, disclose that and return manual status/cancel
41: commands; do not claim that a monitor was registered. Frozen author/proof/reviewer
42: stages perform only their assigned roles and never schedule owner monitoring or
43: redispatch the workflow.
44: 
45: For missing external originals, follow [ordered source retrieval](nl0/references/source-retrieval.md):
46: arXiv, Google full-text search, Google DOI discovery, then confirmed-DOI Sci-Hub
47: lookup with ordinary browser readback when needed. Reuse an already available
48: adequate primary source; retrieval alone does not establish theorem fidelity.
49: At invocation disclose the [conditional-source policy](nl0/references/conditional-sources.md):
50: inaccessible primary texts can permit continued work from complete explicit
51: secondary statements, but the final result remains conditional. Show each
52: actual warning and include warn.json/warn.md in the final report. Never label
53: unverified sources or a qualified workflow as an ordinary full PASS.
54: 
55: Default permanent output is `<problem-directory>/rigorous-proof/<run-id>/`,
56: outside the installed skill. Multiple problems own separate outputs, contexts,
57: queues and ledgers. Use normal local repair unless a first-pass measurement is
58: explicitly requested. Runtime and software controls are fully inside this skill;
59: no repository example/support directory or old test result is required.
60: New jobs retain an allowlisted executable/rule/catalog snapshot in their owned
61: `runtime/` directory and launch from it. Installation updates cannot silently
62: change an active job's bound code; snapshot tampering still fails validation.
63: Historical jobs without snapshots retain their original binding checks.
64: Each native Lean call defaults to a five-minute wall limit. Yui proof workers
65: automatically receive frozen ST020 repair advice after a verified native
66: wall/heartbeat limit, through the same failed tool result. Keep the target and
67: inputs unchanged, repair in the same worker, and recheck. General strategy-bank
68: queries remain optional; this failure-triggered advice needs no extra model call.
69: Follow [fault treatment and authorized exit](nl0/references/error-lifecycle.md).
70: Local Python retries recognized temporary service/network faults every 60seconds,
71: at most 30 times in the same carrier/thread. Other faults and exhausted retries
72: enter a retained `PAUSED_ERROR`, notify the owner through local `codex queue`,
73: and wait for an exact-incident operator action. An error never authorizes task
74: termination or workspace deletion. Release only the completed roles at the
75: specified global-pass, all-local-pass, interface-freeze and final-delivery
76: boundaries, after their bound handoffs are saved. Explicit user cancellation or
77: a selected B-final user decision is a separate authority. Keep
78: scientific evidence and the selected profile. A pause is nonterminal: never
79: restart it or delete its monitor. Existing exited-run recovery is historical,
80: not a substitute for live `resume-error` controls.
81: An explicitly authorized `--after-access-restored` continuation separately
82: supports a verified provider HTTP403 stop at the NL0/Audit A boundary. It checks
83: authenticated model metadata without inference before preparation and launch;
84: 403 stays excluded from automatic retries. Preserve old faults/costs and disclose
85: the new runtime and unreleased-author scope in that operation reference.
86: For a previously stopped inherited probe-directory collision, the same operation
87: reference documents a separate guarded `--repair-local-tool` continuation after
88: verified software repair and explicit owner authorization; it restores the saved
89: located author repair rather than restarting the original proof.
90: The separate guarded `--repair-native-cleanup` route supports an actually exited
91: frozen proof queue stopped only by verified native-process cleanup faults. It
92: preserves the exact source/A/interface, rechecks completed local bodies and
93: restores only the failed worker's own bound drafts; never use it to resample a
94: mathematical nonpass or replace live work.
95: 
96: Normal translation requires a separate independent semantic interface review
97: before freezing and proof dispatch. Normal final Audit B is machine-only: verify
98: that actual E/P, their defining environment and complete proof dependencies still
99: match that reviewed authority. Only a valid-proof/interface-drift exception opens
100: an actual independent B-final model review, with warning-qualified delivery.
101: Follow [proof diagnosis and reviewed repair](nl02lean/references/proof-repair.md).
102: Local compiler defects return to their own author; explicit global proof-connection
103: issues go to the serial connection author. It cannot change frozen E/P or their
104: meaning-determining definitions. No fixed idle-turn threshold retires a round or
105: cancels sibling jobs. Frozen-contract/source defects wait for the user.
106: 
107: 1. **NL0 and Audit A.** Use [Audit A's shared acceptance requirements](nl0/references/audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
108:    as the single mathematical standard for both author and auditor.
109:    Read [the NL0 stage](nl0/references/nl0-stage.md),
110:    [format](nl0/references/nl0-format.md), [self-containment](nl0/references/self-containment.md),
111:    [authoring](nl0/references/nl0-authoring.md), and Audit A's role-specific execution protocol.
112:    Read [external-source review](nl0/references/external-theorems.md) for citations
113:    and [logical packaging](nl0/references/logical-rules.md) for local assumptions.
114:    Use `nl0/scripts/nl0.py`; its explicit accounting is not a mathematical prover.
115:    Controllers and reviewers follow [completion and local repair](nl0/references/review-execution.md)
116:    for global-first parallel R coverage, exact evidence inheritance and stage boundaries.
117: 2. **Translate an accepted NL0 and run Audit B.** Verify the supplied Audit A
118:    authority and exact source version first; do not reconstruct or re-audit an
119:    unchanged proof. Start with [minimal translation](nl02lean/references/minimal-translation.md).
120:    Read [translation](nl02lean/references/stage.md),
121:    [the working sequence](nl02lean/references/integrated-workflow.md), and
122:    [Audit B](nl02lean/references/audit-b.md). Operators use
123:    [execution and file-based control](nl02lean/references/execution-protocol.md)
124:    for parallel queues, status and stops; workers need only their frozen packet.
125:    After local proofs complete, the controller first attempts mechanical
126:    [assembly and source-facing export](nl02lean/references/assembly.md).
127:    Use the serial connection author only for actual connection/library-discharge
128:    repair. Normal final machine Audit B inherits the frozen semantic review;
129:    B-final is reserved for proof-valid interface deviation.
130:    Use
131:    `nl02lean/scripts/source_preparation.py` for bounded shared extraction,
132:    then `workflow.py` for source/IR freeze, proof work and final gates.
133: 3. **Full workflow.** Complete track one, then track two. A changed mathematical
134:    statement or new theorem returns to the affected NL0/Audit A boundary.
135: 
136: ## Mathematical invariants
137: 
138: - Accepted NL0 is a complete natural-language proof relative to explicit H/E/M,
139:   fixed logic and its hash-bound verified background supplement. Important
140:   tools remain explicit; ordinary correct elementary reasoning needs no
141:   exhaustive calculation chain. See [background notes](nl0/references/background-notes.md).
142: - Within NL0, each inference uses only its direct inputs, global definitions and explicitly
143:   established in-scope local facts or positively checked node-local background
144:   notes. Notes never add H or repair a substantive gap. Source papers and producer proof bodies do
145:   not fill gaps in a task packet.
146: - Preserve one global mathematical identity while allowing local Lean views.
147:   Actual cross-view conversions need checked proofs. In stage two, the pinned
148:   Mathlib environment is freely available without NL0 M registration.
149: - Shared mathematical extraction is a bounded local change at translation entry.
150:   Review its new producer and substitution cuts; inherit unchanged evidence.
151:   Freeze the revised NL0 before final IR and worker packets.
152: - Local conditional bodies may run concurrently. Assembly must discharge every
153:   internal dependency with an actual checked proof; conditional checks alone
154:   are not a final result.
155: - The independent pre-freeze review checks every E and complete P, including
156:   hypotheses, quantifiers and relevant definitions. Final machine Audit B checks
157:   actual exported full types and complete closure against that frozen authority.
158:   Supply short direct/equivalent correspondence explanations. Check actual Lean
159:   closure and trust, without a Mathlib-to-NL0 use ledger.
160:   Neither author notes nor a compiler pass are semantic approval.
161: - Stop on a judged substantive mathematical gap. Ordinary expansion and local
162:   verifiable corrections remain allowed. Difficulty or elapsed time does not
163:   establish that a mathematical claim is false.
164: 
165: ## Clean execution and accounting
166: 
167: Operators use [execution terminology](nl0/references/terminology.md) to distinguish
168: Codex conversations, native subagents, Yui jobs, worker slots and controllers.
169: Use the logical phase names **NL0 worker**, **preprocessing worker**,
170: **formalization workers (N slots)** and **postprocessing worker**. A logical
171: worker may contain several separate author/reviewer threads and program steps;
172: N limits concurrent local R reviews and local Lean proof jobs in their separate phases.
173: Report executor termination separately from mathematical acceptance.
174: 
175: Read [isolation](nl0/references/isolation.md) and [measurement](nl0/references/measurement.md)
176: before any model test or benchmark. Run model authoring, planning, proof and
177: review stages through the isolated carrier. The interactive developer's memory,
178: other personal skills, expert packages, old task outputs and hidden reference
179: proofs are never an input source for these stages.
180: 
181: The Yui arm receives only the declared Yui rules and task material. The direct
182: arm receives a minimal task/tool contract and the same mathematical inputs,
183: without Yui planning, strategy or shared-proof guidance. Log actual transmitted
184: instructions, complete allowed inputs, tool schemas/results, model identity,
185: phase, usage and health. Never execute model-generated Python or shell text.
186: 
187: Collect the active phase profiles as described above. `config.json` supplies
188: defaults only when explicitly selected. The current isolated carrier supports
189: Standard speed and checks model/effort availability without fallback. Freeze
190: and record each stage's selected profile;
191: never silently substitute a stronger model or fallback.
192: Resolve the confirmed concurrency before dispatch and record its basis; do not
193: claim an unknown backend maximum. N limits local R-node reviews, then local
194: Lean proof jobs in a later phase. NL0 authoring, global Audit A, preparation,
195: interface work, assembly and Audit B use one serial lane per case.
196: Count root/controller, worker, review and retry calls. Cached/reasoning tokens
197: are subsets of input/output totals, not extra tokens. Missing usage is unknown.
198: 
199: Return the exact accepted scope, source/formal artifacts, unresolved citations
200: or gaps, actual execution health, time/token breakdown, and reproducible commands.

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.
168: 
169: ## Input status
170: 
171: This file fixes the problem, conventions and supplied proof route for future
172: tests. It is a natural-language input, not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
173: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must independently produce
174: and check those artifacts. The basic Hausdorff-measure and integration facts
175: used here must be registered by that future NL0/Audit A workflow.

1: # NL0 data contract, version 2
2: 
3: This document specifies representation. Mathematical acceptance comes from
4: [Audit A's shared requirements](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements).
5: The clean carrier binds the shared section/version/hash in execution and
6: author-readiness records; these are controller records, not extra proof axioms
7: or new fields to invent inside spec/graph.
8: 
9: New graphs/specifications use v2 and audit records use v3. The existing v1
10: Koch/BO cases are historical snapshots and have not been reaccepted. Reading
11: them requires `--legacy`; current default checks reject them. Historical
12: receipt validity is labeled `LEGACY-*` and `current_standard_receipt_valid`
13: remains false. Do not mechanically bump a version number to migrate a proof.
14: Apply [self-containment](self-containment.md) to the actual mathematical text.
15: 
16: ## Authority and semantics
17: 
18: The isolated authoring carrier offers `check_draft` and `submit_draft`, taking
19: an `artifact` JSON object directly. Prefer these to the compatible older
20: `artifact_json` string wrappers: an additional string-encoding layer is not
21: part of the mathematical format. Both routes execute identical checks.
22: 
23: `spec.json` freezes the original full theorem, the conclusion under its declared
24: parameters/hypotheses, the exact H list, global definition pairs, logic policy,
25: source-input hashes, and Lean/mathlib pins. A human must confirm that this
26: specification matches the original problem; string equality cannot establish
27: semantic fidelity. `nl0.json` references this spec by its SHA256 and duplicates
28: none of its definitions or H statements. One separate spec is required per
29: target. Multiple-target decomposition is outside version 2.
30: 
31: Read a derived proposition as a theorem under the original parameters and the
32: H nodes actually used on its derivation path. All additional free variables are
33: locally quantified in its statement; there are no ambient undeclared claims.
34: An unused original H is allowed and reported; do not silently strengthen or
35: weaken the frozen theorem. E/M results retain their general signatures; apply
36: them through explicit bindings and hypothesis checks in the inference.
37: 
38: Graph vertices are propositions and inferences. Edges are generated only as
39: `input proposition -> inference -> output proposition`. An inference requires
40: all inputs. List order is presentation only: a dependency may occur later in
41: the JSON array, provided the graph admits a topological order. Actual circular
42: dependencies, unknown IDs, and disconnected retained branches fail.
43: 
44: The isolated authoring carrier also reports a hash-bound machine checkpoint of
45: its latest own draft and actual structural result. After a context reset, resume
46: that candidate with `read_draft`/`base_candidate`; do not claim no draft exists or
47: restart the frozen input accidentally. The checkpoint grants no Audit A verdict.
48: 
49: ## Specification fields
50: 
51: Use [the authoring template](../templates/authoring.md) and the complete
52: [model-visible submission example](../templates/submission-example.md). The

102: Definitions may be globally visible but guarded. Example: “K is the unique

109: ## Proposition fields
110: 
111: Every proposition has `id`, `kind`, the complete `statement`, `definitions`
112: (D IDs), `binders`, and `objects`:
113: 
114: - `binders`: `{symbol, type}` records for statement-bound variables. These do
115:   not introduce free variables in a consuming R. Register actual nested scope
116:   in the statement; alpha-rename to avoid global shadowing.
117: - `objects`: distinct names of mathematical objects actually used in the
118:   statement, from frozen parameters/primitives, referenced D closure or these
119:   binders. A D also has these fields for its defining expression.
120: 
121: These are inventories, not a parser-generated list. Audit A must find omitted
122: objects by reading actual prose/formulas. Export all formulas and conditions;
123: another N ID or an original equation number cannot replace their content.
124: 
125: | kind | ID | Producer | Additional fields |
126: |---|---|---|---|
127: | `hypothesis` | Hddd | none | exactly matches frozen H statement |
128: | `mathlib` | Mddd | none | `source` record below |
129: | `external` | Eddd | none | `source` record below |
130: | `internal` | Nddd | exactly one | `origin` locating source or explaining added bridge |
131: | `target` | P | exactly one | exact frozen `conclusion` |

133: A source record contains `statement` (exact NL restatement), `evidence` (file
134: hashes), and `hypotheses` (complete applicability obligations, not their proof).
135: M additionally has `declaration`, `module`, `mathlib_commit`, `source_path`,
136: `source_sha256`, `signature` (complete Lean output), and `declaration_kind` equal
137: to `theorem` or `proved_instance`. A definition/opaque constant is not a proved
138: source proposition. Library definitions belong in D. A named M's official
139: library dependencies need not be copied into the project graph; pin the library
140: and inspect relevant axioms. Do not introduce project results as library M.
141: M evidence includes the successful version-1 report from `probe_mathlib.py`,
142: with the same ID, declaration, full signature, source bytes and toolchain pins.
143: In the clean Yui NL0 carrier, `probe_library` produces this evidence and the
144: submission adapter binds exact signature/source metadata from the successful
145: probe matching the selected M ID and actual declaration selector. Those metadata
146: fields may be omitted from that tool's submitted JSON; canonical graph files
147: still contain them in full. No unprobed source is filled from model memory.
148: The clean probe resolves genuine aliases to their canonical kernel name and
149: discovers the actual defining module. A requested module is only a locator
150: hint; its correction is recorded, never silently treated as source evidence.
151: Native type printing (and the legacy `#check @declaration` probe) preserves the complete outer telescope,
152: including implicit/typeclass conditions, using ordinary notation for nested
153: structure applications. Recursive expansion of inherited structure arguments
154: is unnecessary; omitted hypotheses or ellipsis are not permitted. The actual
155: kernel declaration kind, axioms, source bytes and version pins remain evidence.
156: For a local development revision the same tool also accepts
157: `{base_input: "declared-task-ID.json", patches: [...]}` when that explicit frozen
158: task document contains `{spec, graph}`. Patches are JSON data operations
159: `add`, `remove`, `replace`, or `test`, each with an absolute JSON pointer inside
160: `/spec/...` or `/graph/...` and a `value` except for `remove`. Array append uses
161: `/-`. An additional `replace_text` operation has `path`, `old` and `new`
162: instead of `value`: it replaces exactly one nonempty literal occurrence inside
163: an existing string. Missing or ambiguous matches are rejected; this is not a
164: regular expression or executable code. It preserves the rest of a long proof
165: paragraph without asking the model to retype it.
166: Every submission starts from the immutable named input, not the previous
167: failed candidate. The controller records the base hash and actual edits, then
168: performs the identical full source/structure checks. Successful output is still
169: the complete canonical `{spec,graph}`. This is an authoring convenience for
170: unaccepted candidates, not an incremental Audit A receipt or permission to
171: modify accepted/frozen source during a translation run. Actual mathematical
172: changes still invalidate affected reviews.
173: Within the same authoring stage, an actual check also returns its
174: `candidate_number`. Use `{base_candidate: N, patches: [...]}` to revise that
175: exact checked draft, including a structurally rejected draft. `read_draft`
176: can inspect a narrow JSON pointer in that own draft. These are the model's
177: own prior submissions plus bound metadata, not other tasks or local files.
178: Every edit still undergoes the full checker, and no draft inherits acceptance.
179: Resubmit an exact own draft with `{accept_candidate: N}` after a successful

181: explicit `reset_base: true`; this deliberately discards accumulated edits.
182: Without that explicit reset, use `base_candidate` so a later bookkeeping fix

184: The adapter does not rewrite mathematical statements, hypotheses, definitions,
185: binders or arguments. Their fidelity remains the author's and auditor's work.
186: The following two explicit serialization forms copy the author's declared
187: data; they do not infer mathematics or grant Audit A acceptance:
188: 
189: - An S `text`, D `definition`, or `spec.hypotheses[i].statement` may be `{from_task: "declared-input-ID", start_line: 10,
190:   end_line: 20}`. The controller copies exactly those inclusive lines of the
191:   already frozen same-stage input into an ordinary canonical string. It stores

193:   Only these proof/definition/hypothesis text fields have this form;
194:   undeclared files, other tasks and old candidates are not source IDs. Read the

251: ## Inference fields
252: 
253: Required fields: `id: Rddd`, `inputs` (unique proposition IDs), `output` (one
254: N/P ID), `definitions` (direct D references), `rules` (permitted logic-rule
255: names), `locals`, `argument`, and `applications`.
256: 
257: - `locals`: `{symbol, type, scope}` records. Scope identifies a binding inside
258:   this inference; names cannot shadow globals. Two bindings in different
259:   scopes/nodes may use the same spelling. Bound variables of source theorems
260:   can be alpha-renamed and instantiated. Audit actual binding/freshness.
261:   In v2 also require `start`, `end` (inclusive S IDs), `kind` (`arbitrary`,
262:   `definition`, or `witness`), `declaration` (full introduction), `from_inputs`,
263:   `from_local` (prior F IDs) and `objects` (already available objects used to
264:   introduce this one). A witness must have an input/local existence basis.
265:   The checker verifies declared availability/order, not the existence claim's
266:   semantics. Source-bound variables need a legitimate local instantiation.
267:   The `scope` label and inclusive start/end must agree with the prose. Keep an
268:   object live through its last actual use. Establish an existence F in an
269:   earlier S, then choose its witness in a subsequent S; using a newly produced
270:   F as the witness basis in the same paragraph is a forward reference.
271: - `argument`: ordered records `{id: Sddd, text, uses, uses_local, objects,
272:   produces, introduces, discharges}`. S IDs are inference-local and unique. `uses`
273:   lists direct graph inputs used at this point. Local facts established earlier
274:   in the prose do not become graph inputs. The union of `uses` must equal
275:   `inputs`. A citation's presence is not semantic evidence that it was used.
276:   `uses_local` lists only earlier F IDs; `objects` lists the actually used
277:   global/active local objects. `produces` holds complete local facts
278:   `{id: Fddd, statement, binders, objects, assumptions}`; assumptions lists remaining
279:   local L IDs on which the fact depends. A local fact cannot be used before
280:   its production or outside its assumption/object scope. A paragraph cannot
281:   cite its newly produced F as a previous premise. Formulas to be reused by a
282:   different R must appear in the exported proposition, not only in `produces`.
283: - `introduces`/`discharges`: lists of inference-local assumption IDs (e.g.
284:   `L1`). Temporary assumptions are never proposition vertices. Every introduced
285:   ID is unique in this inference and must be discharged once, no earlier than
286:   introduction. These lists account for prose; Audit A checks the actual
287:   formula, scope, and chosen rule. A correctly closed implication may retain
288:   the assumption in its antecedent. Deleting the ID cannot justify an output.
289: - `applications`: records covering every directly used E/M input, with
290:   `{input, at: Sddd, bindings, hypothesis_checks}`.
291:   `bindings` is a nonempty string spelling out the actual variable/parameter
292:   substitution; it is not a JSON mapping. `hypothesis_checks` is an ordered
293:   list of nonempty strings, one per declared source obligation. For example,
294:   `"bindings": "Set the source parameter a to the current x."` records a
295:   substitution; it does not prove its conditions.
296:   The S paragraph must list
297:   this input in `uses`; only local facts available before that paragraph may
298:   supply application conditions. E applications additionally require
299:   an inference-local unique `id: Addd`; different actual uses of the same E
300:   need separate IDs and records. M may also use explicit A IDs for repeated
301:   instances; a legacy M without `id` uses its input ID as the unique key.
302:   `hypothesis_checks` has one nonempty
303:   explanation for each corresponding source obligation. A hypothesis needs an
304:   actual argument from inputs/H/local proved facts; filling a string is only
305:   an accounting check. Prove substantive normalization bridges as N nodes.
306: 
307: Input-free R nodes are permitted only for explicitly shown calculations or
308: logical/definitional consequences. They are audited proofs, not a fourth kind
309: of trusted source. Transitive inputs need not be repeated unless used directly.
310: 
311: ## Audit record
312: 
313: `audit-a.json` contains `format_version`, `graph_sha256`, `spec_sha256`,
314: `reviewer` (`identity`, `mode`, `independent`, `disclosure`), `target_review`,
315: `definition_reviews`, `source_reviews`, and `inference_reviews`.
316: 
317: Each review contains `verdict: PASS|FAIL|UNVERIFIED`, substantive `notes`, and
318: hashed `evidence`. Inference reviews contain ten separate check review objects:
319: `inputs`, `argument`, `dependency_accounting`, `output`, `scope`, `applicability`,
320: `statement_closure`, `object_closure`, `dependency_closure`, `packet_replay`.
321: Each check has `{verdict, notes, evidence, locations}`. `locations` contains
322: JSON pointers resolving inside that R's actual packet, such as
323: `/inputs/0/statement` or `/inference/argument/1/text`. PASS requires at least
324: one actual inspected location; a boolean/enum alone is insufficient.
325: Every D, every E/M source, every R, and the target must be covered exactly once.
326: Spec input hashes and source evidence are read back; malformed/duplicate JSON
327: keys, missing files, changed bytes, failed verdicts, and stale audit hashes fail.
328: 
329: Use audit `format_version: 3` for all new records. Audit v1/v2 are readable
330: only with historical graph v1 and `--legacy`; they cannot satisfy this contract.
331: Each E source review additionally has `citation_checks`, mapping exactly
332: `literature_identity`, `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`,
333: `context_completeness`, `version_and_eligibility` to separate ordinary review
334: objects `{verdict, notes, evidence}`.
335: Each version-3 inference review additionally has `external_applications`,
336: mapping exactly its E application A IDs to records
337: `{input, verdict, notes, evidence, bindings_review, hypothesis_reviews,
338: conclusion_review, bridges}`. `input` must match A's E; each nested review
339: has `{verdict, notes, evidence}`; the ordered `hypothesis_reviews` list matches
340: all source obligations one for one. `bridges` lists N nodes already in R's
341: direct input list. A bridge string is not a proof of that bridge.
342: 
343: Each inference review also has `replay: {packet_sha256, mode, carrier,
344: prior_exposure, read_materials}`. Modes are `unperformed`,
345: `same_context_diagnostic`, and `fresh_packet_only`. A passing replay/overall
346: inference requires the actual fresh carrier, empty prior proof exposure, and
347: `read_materials` equal to `["packet:<hash>"]` for mathematical input. Skill
348: instructions supply the procedure, not additional mathematics. The hash must
349: match the regenerated packet. Keep traces as evidence; metadata cannot
350: authenticate a claimed identity or prove truthful isolation.
351: 
352: `audit-template` creates only UNVERIFIED reviews, empty check locations and an
353: unperformed replay. It refuses to overwrite an existing output. It does not
354: inherit author notes or old verdicts. `inspect-audit` can inspect this pending
355: record; `check --audit` rejects it. Each PASS must come from actual review.
356: 
357: `check --audit` accepts only fully passing records. `inspect-audit --audit`
358: also validates the completeness and evidence of FAIL/UNVERIFIED records and
359: returns their unresolved review paths; success of inspection is not proof
360: acceptance. Overall PASS with a failed child review never passes acceptance.
361: 
362: Mode `same_context_self_audit` requires `independent: false`. If claiming an
363: independent review, disclose its actual carrier and input boundary; this file
364: does not authenticate identity or prove independence.
365: 
366: ## Local packet
367: 
368: The v2 packet contains `contract_version`, `case_id`, spec/graph hashes,
369: parameters, fixed logic, pins, expanded definitions, complete input/output
370: ports, the current inference, a warning, and `packet_sha256`. Source ports keep
371: applicability obligations and M signatures; primary-document verification is
372: separate. Producer arguments, original-proof locations, source proof text,
373: non-input H and extra ancestor/guard statements are not supplied. Guards must
374: already be direct inputs. The packet intentionally omits the global full target
375: so that its unstated premises cannot become an ambient local hypothesis.
376: 
377: Its digest is SHA256 of UTF-8 canonical JSON (`sort_keys=True`,
378: `ensure_ascii=False`, `separators=(",", ":")`) excluding `packet_sha256`.
379: It is independent of audit-verdict fields, avoiding a circular receipt hash.
380: Packets are generated views and never a second editable proof authority.
381: 
382: ## Mechanical boundaries
383: 
384: The checker validates declared objects, the frozen contract, graph closure,
385: notation-name metadata, citation parity, local-assumption accounting, guarded
386: definition availability, and hash-bound audit coverage. It verifies source
387: checkout/file hashes, not the truth of a source restatement. The printed
388: signature must be obtained from a successful pinned Lean probe and compared by
389: the auditor; an arbitrary string called `signature` is not verification.
390: 
391: The checker cannot establish that a natural-language formula is well typed,
392: that two spellings have the same mathematical meaning, that a hidden theorem
393: was not used, that a local witness did not escape the prose, or that an argument
394: is valid. Those are explicit Audit A obligations. Neither a JSON PASS nor a
395: fabricated complete audit receipt is a mathematical certificate.
396: Numbered-reference diagnostics reject common opaque references, not every
397: possible paraphrase or hidden import. Behavioral tests must actually ask an
398: auditor to review unseen controls; manually prefilled FAIL records only test
399: receipt rejection and must be reported as such.
400: 
401: ## Verified background receipt extension
402: 
403: New receipts declare `background_policy: "verified-background-1"`. Each R review
404: may contain `background_notes`, with fields in background-notes.md. These are
405: actual reviewer judgments, not unverified extra hypotheses. Old consumers must
406: reject unsupported fields rather than silently drop them. The authored graph
407: remains unchanged. A new replay uses `fresh_packet_with_verified_background`
408: and binds `library_evidence` plus its actual material hashes; old strict
409: empty-note records can retain `fresh_packet_only`.
410: 
411: `nl0.validate` returns the note supplement/hash and note count. A packet read
412: from an accepted source includes its notes and the original reviewed-packet
413: hash. This enriched view is not claimed to be the original replay input.
414: Translation binds the supplement in `contract.source.background_supplement_sha256`.
415: 
416: The interface source also retains the complete `background_supplement`, not
417: just its hash. Plan steps list the relevant qualified note IDs, for example
418: `background_notes:["R004.BG001"]`. Workflow freeze checks the paragraph mapping;
419: local Lean packets receive only their selected notes.

1: # Ordered retrieval of external theorem sources
2: 
3: Use this procedure for each literature E whose original text is missing. Both
4: the NL0 author and global Audit A reviewer follow it. Reuse an already supplied,
5: hash-bound primary document instead of downloading it again. The invoking agent
6: may retrieve sources before dispatch, but every supplied document must be an
7: explicit input; never insert files into an active run's frozen inputs.
8: 
9: ## 1. Identify the requested work and edition
10: 
11: Read the actual citation and its use in the supplied proof. Record author,
12: title, known arXiv ID/version or DOI, source kind, and expected theorem/lemma,
13: page or equation. Search terms must come from that material. Do not invent an
14: identifier or accept a nearby search hit. A shared title does not establish
15: that two editions have the same statements or numbering.
16: 
17: ## 2. Try arXiv first
18: 
19: Call `search_external_sources(query=title_and_authors, engine="arxiv")`. If an
20: arXiv ID is already given, use that exact ID, including its version suffix.
21: Read the matching abstract/version record, then use `read_external_source` on
22: the actual PDF link. The search tool exposes PDF locators from arXiv abstract
23: links; those locators are not a substitute for downloading the PDF.
24: 
25: Check identity, version, page count and the complete relevant result. Follow
26: its definitions and standing hypotheses. If only another version is available,
27: compare the relevant statements and their conventions, or continue searching
28: for the cited edition. Never copy a page number from a different version.
29: Stop retrieval when an adequate original has actually been obtained.
30: 
31: ## 3. Search Google for the complete text
32: 
33: If the needed original is still missing, call
34: `search_external_sources(query=title_and_authors, engine="google")`. Open
35: plausible author, institution, repository or publisher links and download the
36: full document with `read_external_source`. A title-only result, catalog,
37: abstract, search snippet or AI overview does not verify an external theorem.
38: 
39: For `BROWSER_REQUIRED` or a verification page, retry the same search/read with
40: `browser=true`. The controller can use an installed, isolated local Chrome
41: through the fixed optional helper. It performs real navigation and rendered
42: readback, preserves screenshots and uses no personal browser profile. This
43: also works for CLI stages without a desktop tab-control tool. Missing browser
44: dependencies, unresolved challenges and browser failures are explicit records;
45: they do not stop the mathematical workflow by themselves.
46: 
47: An invoking agent with an actual built-in-browser control tool may instead use
48: that frontend and stage the downloaded original before dispatch. Opening or
49: queuing a tab alone is never readback evidence. Do not claim that a headless
50: Chrome session is the user's visible in-app tab.
51: 
52: ## 4. Find and confirm a DOI, then try Sci-Hub
53: 
54: When full text remains missing, search Google again using the exact title,
55: authors and `DOI`. Inspect `doi_candidates` and the linked publisher or DOI
56: metadata; confirm title, author and edition. These strings are only candidate
57: identifiers. Reuse a DOI already established by the supplied bibliography or
58: matching primary metadata; a blocked Google page need not prevent that lookup.
59: Do not guess a DOI or request an unrelated article just to make retrieval pass.
60: 
61: Call `search_external_sources(query=confirmed_doi, engine="scihub", browser=true)`.
62: The controller navigates to `https://sci-hub.box/<DOI>`. Ordinary site controls,
63: including its own ALTCHA verification button when present, may complete normal
64: access. Follow the returned PDF/object link through `read_external_source`.
65: Record any redirect, including a different mirror's final hostname, rather
66: than claiming the bytes came from the initial host. Do not fabricate challenge
67: tokens, import personal cookies, silently purchase access or change system
68: proxy settings. If a challenge cannot be completed normally, retain the failure
69: and move to the disclosed conditional route.
70: 
71: ## 5. Establish source fidelity after retrieval
72: 
73: Retain the actual URL, final URL, retrieval timestamp, document/text hashes and
74: access receipt. A fetched PDF is a readable source candidate, not an automatic
75: truth or theorem-fidelity judgment. Apply [external-theorem review](external-theorems.md):
76: confirm author/title/version, locate the result, read the full statement and
77: governing definitions, check corrections/version history where available, and
78: map every hypothesis, conclusion and constant dependency to E. Each application
79: still needs its own verified substitutions and premise checks. A source that
80: states a different theorem is a mismatch, not an inaccessible-text deferral.
81: 
82: For a changed edition, retain both document hashes and a locator/statement map.
83: Do not silently substitute the journal version for a cited preprint. Any

90: present in a declared secondary input, its input ID and own failed
91: `access_records` paths. An unavailable original does not justify inventing a
92: statement from memory or treating a known contradiction as an assumption.
93: If the statement itself is missing or incomplete, identify that missing content
94: instead of pretending the source-only route closes the proof.

96: Retain `UNVERIFIED_PRIMARY`, `warn.json` and `warn.md`. Continue all other
97: mathematical, Lean, assembly and audit work normally. The final result remains
98: `WORKFLOW-CONDITIONAL` (or the corresponding stage's conditional status) until
99: the actual source and affected review are completed. Display each warning to
100: the user when it arises and in the final answer. A compile pass does not remove
101: source uncertainty. Do not repeat indefinitely an unchanged blocked query;
102: preserve its failure and advance to the next route.

1: # Construct NL0 against Audit A
2: 
3: [Audit A's shared requirements](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
4: are the sole mathematical acceptance authority. This document is an execution
5: guide. Follow the table IDs, not an independently maintained approximation of
6: what the auditor might want. The clean carrier supplies that exact frozen
7: section to both roles. [The schema](nl0-format.md) describes serialization;
8: [the author template](../templates/authoring.md) gives tool shapes and examples.
9: The elementary permissions come from the same controller-owned foundation.
10: Use ordinary rigorous mathematical granularity. Explicitly register important
11: tools; eligible tiny background uses can be checked and recorded by Audit A
12: under [verified-background admission](background-notes.md). Do not pre-emptively
13: rebuild elementary theories or treat an omitted basic M ID as a substantive gap.
14: 
15: ## 1. Understand and freeze the supplied work
16: 
17: Read the original target and entire supplied proof. Identify its phases and
18: potential gaps, without adopting an alternative research route. Extract the
19: original H, parameters and definition pairs into spec.json. Preserve their
20: source locations. This supplies the `target` check; naming a condition inside
21: a parameter type does not satisfy its H inventory. Inspect material endpoint,
22: zero-object and ambient-dimension cases before building the graph.
23: Each H must itself state the complete given condition; phrases such as
24: "as specified in the target" do not supply that condition to a packet reader.
25: When an original GIVEN passage is already adequate, select its exact frozen
26: lines for `spec.hypotheses[i].statement`, using the same literal binding as D
27: definitions and S text. Preserve its origin and distinguish original givens
28: from desired conclusions and claims established later in the proof. Copying
29: does not turn those latter claims into hypotheses or certify fidelity.
30: 
31: Inventory each object's construction guards before exporting it with a type.
32: If a guard is a result of this work, establish it in an earlier N producer
33: before using the guarded D; do not promise that a later argument will make the
34: current declaration well-defined. Alternatively specify an actually total
35: construction and prove its intended property separately. Do not add a missing
36: guard as an original H. This is graph organization along the given proof,
37: not permission to change that proof or its hypotheses.
38: When the original already gives a complete adequate definition, use the
39: explicit frozen-input line binding for D.definition if helpful. This preserves
40: the selected text and its provenance without granting a property. Rewriting
41: notation still requires a complete faithful definition and its declarations.
42: Use the [complete neutral construction pattern](../templates/guarded-definition-example.md)
43: when P includes both a well-definedness claim and a property of the object:
44: prove the guard without the object, then use that guard as a direct input to
45: the object-using inference. A global list's textual order is not graph order.
46: 
47: ## 2. Design outputs from their consumers
48: 
49: Follow the existing proof phases to choose N/R units. Work backward from P:
50: what exact formulas, maps, parameter ranges and representation identifications
51: will each consumer actually use? Put those in its input proposition's exported
52: statement. Read that statement without the producer body. If the consumer
53: cannot reconstruct a needed fact from it, enlarge the producer's proved
54: output or give the consumer another genuine direct input. Then write the
55: producer under precisely its inputs. This implements `statement_closure`,
56: `inputs` and `output`; it is not permission to invent a stronger theorem.
57: 
58: Start another S when the local parameters or purpose change; export a reused
59: result as N and a within-R result as a complete F. Avoid one giant copied S
60: followed by a long sequence of isolated symbol patches. Copy exact supplied
61: calculations through task-line text binding when helpful, then close the
62: copied unit's actual declarations and premises. Keep all required coefficients,
63: normalizations, limiting arguments and exceptional cases.
64: Retain every calculation needed for P and the supplied core route. An
65: independent optional comment/corollary outside that dependency may be omitted;
66: note a material omission in the existing context note. This never licenses
67: dropping a needed derivation or weakening an output. Any retained claim must
68: itself have its complete grounds.
69: 
70: ## 3. Construct the proof and its factual grounds together
71: 
72: An isomorphism or structural identification supplies its stated maps and
73: relations, not every subsequent dimension/rank claim by name alone. For a
74: needed count, display the basis, spanning/independence and finite count, or
75: invoke an appropriate verified source. Likewise regularity closure and
76: differentiation rules need their actual grounds; a familiar operation name
77: does not extend the fixed calculation profile. Prefer an adequate verified
78: background input to unnecessarily rebuilding its whole theory.
79: 
80: For each S, identify its substantive direct inputs and local grounds while
81: writing. Ordinary correct elementary reasoning may be compressed; tiny basic
82: library uses may receive verified audit notes. Check the
83: unit at that point; do not postpone its source inventory until after the whole
84: proof. Read `dependency_closure`, `argument`, `dependency_accounting` and
85: `scope` as construction obligations, not final assurances to fill in later.
86: 
87: If a fact needs an M/E, inspect the real pinned/primary source, register its
88: full contract, and write its actual application. Follow `sources` and
89: `applicability`: substitute the actual function/domain/scalars and ground each
90: premise in an available input or displayed derivation. A source-hypothesis
91: field saying a condition holds is not itself a derivation. Prefer an already
92: proved adequate general theorem to rebuilding it. A specialized bridge still
93: needs its local proof. For E follow [external-source review](external-theorems.md).
94: For inaccessible text follow Audit A's [retrieval/deferred checks](audit-a.md#paywalled-or-inaccessible-primary-text).
95: 
96: For M, use the actual pinned declaration as the full source contract, including
97: its binders, implicit arguments and typeclass premises. Do not insert an
98: extra condition into that contract or omit a native premise. Keep a specialized
99: application distinct from the native statement and justify its substitutions.
100: The probe supplies canonical source metadata; it does not discharge the
101: application's premises or certify the local proof.
102: 
103: Write the exact conclusion obtained at an application before using it at a
104: different domain, measure, carrier or codomain. Any restriction, extension or
105: identification requires its own available ground. If instead deriving a fact
106: by a named property's definition, supply that definition and display the
107: instantiated clause and ensuing reasoning. Do not register a new source just
108: because a fully displayed definition-based derivation also has a standard
109: name. Prove each added consequence under all its cases; omit an unnecessary
110: extra claim rather than leave its proof incomplete.
111: 
112: Introduce an auxiliary object at its actual first use, with its kind,
113: existence basis and scope. Keep object dependencies in `objects` and earlier
114: proof IDs in `from_local`. Preserve the object's type and all uses when
115: renaming it. Apply `definitions` and `object_closure` to the actual prose.
116: Use [logical packaging](logical-rules.md) for quantified and conditional work.
117: 
118: ## 4. Inspect the actual stored candidate
119: 
120: Use check_draft for structural feedback and read_draft for actual changed
121: records. Continue from the same-stage candidate after a rejected edit. Stable
122: unique @ID/@symbol selectors are available in own-stage reads/edits, not in
123: Audit A evidence pointers. Format work requires a concrete edit or source
124: query rather than repeated progress reports.
125: For multiline text use read_draft's numbered line view and its complete-string
126: hash with replace_lines; avoid retyping an escaped old paragraph merely to
127: make a small edit. Re-read after a stale hash and use existing @IDs after
128: array changes. No editor infers missing mathematics.
129: 
130: Read each own conditional packet after structural checking. It supplies only
131: that R's actual premises, definitions, fixed logic, output and own argument.
132: Use the shared criteria to inspect these contents, including each output's
133: consumer-facing statement, rather than remembering what the full manuscript
134: or another producer established. This is the same author's inspection, not an
135: extra independent reviewer and not a second Audit A.
136: Apply Audit A's shared scope rule: an actual direct N is assumed in this
137: conditional implication; do not re-prove its producer or read an ancestor
138: body here. The global graph must still contain that producer, and a needed
139: fact absent from the exported statement must be established explicitly.
140: In the existing original_context_note explicitly check the actual D records'
141: types and guards against their available producers, as well as H/target and
142: source fidelity. In the inference notes compare each source's exact delivered
143: conclusion with the next line that consumes it. These are inspections of the
144: stored proof, not another copy of its argument.
145: 
146: Record concise located context/output/inference notes using the existing
147: fields. Their criterion grouping comes directly from Audit A. Report readiness
148: as no_known_issue, unresolved or not_checked and preserve located open issues.
149: A complete set of notes with an unresolved issue cannot release the proof.
150: Resolve it in the actual stored argument, or explicitly justify withdrawing
151: an erroneous self-finding; reference the resolution location. Do not erase an
152: old issue by omitting it. Python validates these states and bindings, not the
153: truth of the author's mathematical judgment. A claim of no_known_issue can
154: still fail the subsequent independent Audit A.
155: 
156: ### Routine completion and substantive proof gaps
157: 
158: A needed statement in the supplied proof is initially a proof obligation:
159: derive it locally, export a proved N, or supply an exactly verified source.
160: The fact that the current draft has not done so yet is not a mathematical
161: obstruction. Missing inventory, source registration or exposition is work to
162: complete, not by itself a terminal gap report. If reporting an actual obstacle,
163: identify the concrete implication and the mathematical difficulty encountered
164: during normal understanding, checking and completion, rather than only noting
165: that no proof/source has yet been entered. This imposes no fixed time/attempt
166: count and requires neither a counterexample nor a proof of irreparability.
167: 
168: When writing NL0, expand the argument along the proof strategy already present
169: in the original work. Actively supply routine omitted derivations, correct
170: verifiable typographical errors and non-substantive local mistakes, and write
171: the complete argument into NL0 without interrupting the user for each item.
172: Completion must preserve the original target, the original theorem hypotheses
173: and the core proof strategy.
174: 
175: If a step remains blocked after normal understanding, checking and completion
176: attempts, carefully assess the obstacle: is it work needed for ordinary
177: rigorous expansion, or a substantive gap in the original proof? The model
178: should make this judgment from the mathematical content and actual progress;
179: no fixed elapsed-time limit or attempt count is a mathematical criterion.
180: 
181: If the obstacle is judged to be a substantive proof gap, stop NL0 construction
182: for the current proof, preserve the completed work, and report the gap's
183: location, the unsupported implication and the grounds for that judgment.
184: Do not automatically start new research on the original problem, seek a new
185: core proof strategy, or modify the original theorem to make the proof pass.
186: 
187: Recognizing a gap does not require finding a counterexample or proving that
188: the gap is irreparable. If the only established fact is that completion has
189: not been achieved, and its substantive nature cannot be judged reliably,
190: report an "unresolved suspected proof gap" rather than declaring the original
191: theorem false. Prolonged runtime, network or tool faults, and model capability
192: limitations alone are not evidence of a mathematical error.
193: 
194: In the isolated NL0 carrier, unfinished source registration, JSON bookkeeping or
195: ordinary drafting calls for the next actual query, draft or local edit, not an
196: obstacle report. Keep the own draft and continue within its remaining budget. A
197: terminal mathematical-gap report must identify a genuinely unsupported
198: mathematical implication and its grounds, rather than merely restating that
199: the requested artifact is not finished. A stage outcome is not whole-task
200: completion; ordinary failed candidates return to bounded correction/review.
201: 
202: Incorporate completed corrections into the argument and its actual dependency
203: records. Audit A reviews that revised version; existing hash binding and
204: invalidation rules still apply.
205: 
206: 
207: ## 5. Freeze and hand over
208: 
209: When there is no known unfinished obligation, submit the exact candidate bound
210: to the author notes and shared acceptance version. If the budget ends first,
211: preserve the draft as unfinished; do not call a known-incomplete artifact a
212: complete proof. A diagnostic audit of an unfinished draft, if requested,
213: remains separate from a qualifying first-acceptance audit.
214: 
215: Freeze source/graph hashes and generate views and an UNVERIFIED scaffold.
216: Audit A receives the original problem for fidelity and fresh per-R packets for
217: local replay; it receives no author notes or prior review feedback. Its actual
218: judgments determine acceptance under the same shared criteria. Structural
219: validation, author readiness and mathematical acceptance are distinct results.

1: # Self-containment details
2: 
3: This is the detailed meaning of Audit A's `statement_closure`,
4: `object_closure` and `dependency_closure` requirements. The
5: [shared Audit A section](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
6: is the acceptance authority for author and auditor; this annex supplies
7: interpretation and examples, not an independent permission policy.
8: 
9: ## Two boundaries
10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound verified background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements
14: are fully restated; their primary sources are inspected for provenance, not
15: used to supply unstated premises. The fixed library's own proof dependencies
16: need not be recopied. The target work's internal results must be proved here.
17: 
18: Every R must also be checkable from its packet alone: the complete statements
19: of its direct inputs, their required definitions/declarations, its complete
20: output, its local declarations, and its own argument. Another R's proof body,
21: an ancestor not listed as an input, an ambient original H, an original-source
22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.
23: Whole-target/source-fidelity checks are separate from this local proof check.
24: Under verified-background-1, local review may additionally verify routine
25: pinned-mathlib facts using logged read-only queries and record them in the
26: receipt. They join this R's effective dependencies, without new H or a graph
27: rewrite. See [background notes](background-notes.md). Mathematical uncertainty
28: still blocks; ordinary correct elementary compression alone does not.
29: 
30: Original theorem conditions are H nodes, including conditions that could be
31: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
32: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and
33: put its required nonzero condition in H; do not write “nonzero vector” in its
34: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule
35: applies to characteristic/range conditions and equations. An R must list every
36: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed
37: finite-language rules remain available; no new substantive theorem is added.
38: 
39: An output must be understandable and callable without reading its producer's
40: argument. Include the actual equalities/inequalities, binder types, hypotheses,
41: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
42: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
43: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
44: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
45: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.
46: 
47: ## Object closure
48: 
49: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
50: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
51: 
52: 1. A frozen parameter, explicit logical primitive, or global D definition.
53:    State its meaning, type/domain and parameter dependence. Global primitives
54:    cover only core typed syntax, not a dictionary of subject-specific objects.
55:    New subjects use the same parameter/definition/local declaration mechanism;
56:    symbol registration never licenses a theorem.
57: 2. A binder inside the current proposition's full statement. Its scope remains
58:    that statement. A variable bound in an input does not become a free object
59:    in the consuming proof; instantiate the statement explicitly.
60: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact
61:    declaration, introduction basis, and scope. An arbitrary variable requires
62:    legitimate quantifier introduction; a definition uses already available
63:    objects; a witness requires an input or an earlier local existence proof.
64: 
65: A declaration cannot grant existence, uniqueness, invertibility, regularity,
66: or a desired property merely by naming an object. Those obligations require
67: proof. Any D guard needed to use the object must be a direct R input, not a
68: theorem silently recovered from ancestor closure. Record mutually compatible
69: choices and witness dependence. Temporary assumptions stay inside R and must
70: be correctly discharged. Branch witnesses, local facts and local notation
71: cannot escape their scopes. Export a quantified or conditional statement when
72: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy
73: variables may be reused in disjoint local scopes.
74: 
75: ## Dependency closure
76: 
77: Inventory actual factual uses from the prose back to their grounds, not just
78: from an input list forward to a generic `uses` list. Each substantive imported theorem, prior project lemma or original
79: assumption must be a direct input. Eligible omitted basic library uses are
80: recorded as verified audit notes in the effective dependency ledger. A definition supplies meaning, not a theorem. An R output is not its
81: own premise. Adding the desired formula as an unproved input is not a repair.
82: 
83: Explicit local calculations and fully proved intermediate facts may remain
84: inside R. Give a reused local fact a full F statement and identify its earlier
85: derivation and open assumptions. No separate graph vertex is needed for every
86: algebraic equality. A nontrivial imported result cannot be called a local
87: calculation. Substantive reusable lemmas should become N/R pairs; any fact
88: reused by another R must be exported in a complete proposition statement.
89: 
90: The controller owns `spec.logic.calculations` and the small core syntax table
91: (`nl0/scripts/foundations.py`). The clean author tool binds omitted metadata and
92: rejects extra author permissions or task-specific primitives. This fixed
93: language grants no MVT, FTC, Fubini, convergence, compactness or regularity
94: theorem. Such facts need a declared input or an actual local derivation.
95: An author-written permission claim, in any field or prose, has no authority.
96: Ordinary typed arithmetic notation is part of this fixed language: natural
97: numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers mean their standard
98: structures with usual numerals and operations. Finite calculations include
99: their zero/one laws, such as `a+0=a`, as well as explicit algebra/order
100: derivations. Do not demand a separate E/M for an operation token or an allowed
101: finite calculation. This does not grant calculus, topology or measure theorems.
102: Conversely, inspect an actual displayed local derivation before demanding a
103: duplicate E/M input for its conclusion. A named consequence proved by permitted
104: finite algebra/order steps is not an imported premise. If a local derivation
105: fails, locate its unsupported implication rather than its absent theorem name.
106: 
107: Metadata accounts for the argument but never replaces it. Copying all inputs
108: into a single `uses` record, registering a symbol without declaring it in the
109: proof, or writing a PASS label cannot establish closure.
110: 
111: ## Operational acceptance
112: 
113: 1. Author using the node template. Reverse-check the actual prose for missing
114:    declarations, unexpanded references and unlisted facts before freezing.
115: 2. Generate a packet for each R. The v2 generator supplies no original proof,
116:    producer proofs, provenance file locators, extra ancestor statements or
117:    undeclared ambient H. Direct source contracts and required definitions are
118:    included. Packet hashes bind the mathematical input actually reviewed.
119: 3. Review all closure/inference checks, admitting positively checked routine
120:    background notes under the shared policy. Record concrete packet locations and reasons for every verdict.
121: 4. Perform a fresh local replay with disclosed controlled background lookup. The reviewer gets the skill instructions
122:    and that packet plus logged pinned-mathlib queries, without original proof,
123:    other R bodies, author review
124:    notes, old verdicts, or an answer key. Record the actual carrier, packet hash,
125:    prior exposure and mathematical material read. Skill instructions supply no
126:    extra mathematical premise. Do not falsely claim a same-context rereading
127:    is a fresh replay. This rule does not authorize starting a new external
128:    service or agent; if the required carrier has not been used, keep replay
129:    UNVERIFIED and report that limit.
130:    Prior exposure means known task/proof material supplied or read in earlier
131:    contexts; this is not a claim about unknown pretraining contents. Learned
132:    mathematical knowledge cannot replace a missing declared premise or proof.
133: 5. An ineligible missing declaration, missing statement content, unlisted substantive theorem or need
134:    to look outside the packet blocks acceptance. Record the defect; do not
135:    silently repair it while assigning PASS. Return substantive/structural defects to authoring and review the frozen
136:    revision; eligible background notes need no author rewrite. Routine completion does not require a
137:    separate user interruption for every omission. Distinguish a representation
138:    defect from a substantive mathematical gap under the existing gap policy.
139: 
140: The code rejects explicit malformed references, inventories, scopes, guards
141: and receipts. It does not infer hidden hypotheses from property words in types,
142: or decide theorem applications by matching a list of mathematical names.
143: These semantic obligations apply equally to every subject and remain part of
144: author inspection and Audit A. An omitted inventory entry or unnamed
145: theorem hidden in prose still requires actual semantic review. Freshness and
146: truthful reviewer identity need execution evidence; record shape/hashes cannot
147: authenticate them. No natural-language audit is a Lean kernel certificate.

1: # Package local reasoning as true theorem nodes
2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning.
